title: Join a List Into a CSV Line
statement:
Turning a list of fields into one comma-separated line sounds like it should
be a one-liner, and in C# it is -- but only once you have decided what an
empty list is supposed to produce, which is exactly the case a hand-rolled
loop is most likely to get wrong.

## Your function

```
public static string JoinCsv(List<string> items);
```

Return every element of `items` joined by a single comma, with no comma
before the first element or after the last. `items` may be empty; none of
its elements are ever `null`.

## Watch out

- **An empty list joins to the empty string, not to nothing at all and not
  to an error.** `JoinCsv(new List<string>())` returns `""` -- a
  zero-length string is still a string, and is the correct, representable
  answer here.
- **A one-element list has no commas in it.** `JoinCsv(new List<string> {
  "solo" })` returns `"solo"`, not `"solo,"` or `",solo"` -- the comma is a
  *separator* between elements, and one element has no neighbour to be
  separated from.
- A loop that appends `item + ","` after every element and only fixes the
  trailing comma up afterwards works, but there is a single method that
  does the whole job -- and does not need the fix-up in the first place.

tests.name: an empty list joins to the empty string
a single-element list has no commas
